sections.h2: Each EV counts three times, so 5% EVs cut a fleet's counted average by 9.5 g/km

chart.title: Only the threefold count brings a 5% EV fleet near the FY2028 target of 94.8
chart.sub: Counted average for a fleet of 95 petrol cars at 110 g/km and 5 EVs, g CO2/km.
chart.source: The Hindu; Economic Times; Autocar Professional; blog calculation.

sections.means: Counted plainly the fleet averages 104.5 g/km, and India's threefold count brings it to 95.0 g/km.
sections.todo: Regulators should publish how much of each fleet's compliance comes from the EV multiplier and fuel discounts.

sections.h2: Petrol cars may average 127.4 g/km at 10% EVs, up from 95.5 with none

chart.title: Every EV sold lets the petrol cars beside it emit more under the multiplier
chart.sub: Average CO2 allowed for petrol cars on MIDC, g CO2/km, by EV share of the fleet.
chart.source: Blog calculation from the CAFE-III targets and 3× EV multiplier.

sections.means: With no EVs the flexibilities loosen the FY2032 target from 78.9 to about 95.5 g/km, and with 10% EVs the petrol allowance rises to 127.4 g/km.
sections.todo: Test the fleet-average result on the actual tailpipe emissions reported by carmakers, not only on the counted figure.

sections.h2: The 8% E20 discount turns a car tested at 103 g/km into 94.8 on paper

chart.title: The E20 discount lowers the counted figure without changing what the tailpipe emits
chart.sub: One petrol car on E20, g CO2/km.
chart.source: The Hindu; Economic Times; Autocar Professional; this blog's tests.

sections.means: The discount credits the ethanol's carbon as biogenic, so a car tested at 103 g/km is counted as 94.8 g/km.
sections.todo: Require E20 cars to be tested on E20 fuel before the discount is applied to their declared CO2.
